Let users "reblog" or "retweet" stuff. Have this appear in a feed separate from the normal verse

Technically Reddit has this already through the subs /r/bestof and /r/defaultgems. I suppose same subs could be created here and people can choose to subscribe to them or not. I like this option more as it makes it easy to "reblog" posts and comments. Building another type of reblogging feature might be a bit too much work for too little gain.

Hm, so basically, your goal is to turn Voat into another social network?

One of the main advantages of forum type websites was that posts, and not usernames, are the main focus. The type of features you suggest encourage clique building and vote brigade creation, and would probably destroy Voat before it even gets off the ground.

What separates Facebook and Twitter from Reddit? The biggest thing is NO DOWNVOaTING.

Getting rid of downvoats entirely is probably too drastic a measure.

Trying to hide them behind css is a half-assed "no downvoting" option that probably does more harm than good.

How about allowing a maximum downvote percentage? This seems like a fairly easy coding job. Say you allow 20 percent of voats to be downvoats. Every time a user downvoats something, do a simple math check to see if downvoats are over the allowed percentage. You could also reset it once a month or at some interval so that people can't save up their downvoats and use them much later.

Hide a comment's vote count once the difference between upvotes and downvotes is more or less than a certain number. For example, once a comment has 10 more ups than downs, or 10 more downs than ups, make its vote count invisible in the comments thread (but keep displaying it in other places, like the user's comment history). This prevents people from simply voting with the crowd, while keeping vote information accessible in the interest of transparency.

reddit did this, and it's actually what drove a good bit of people here (that and the whole fappening thing). Just from that, I don't think it's a good idea.

Build in some kind of "friending" or "following" feature, so users can choose to get notifications when their friends post content. This would encourage users to interact on a more personal level, since it puts user/user interaction on a level of importance similar to that given to content (you'd get friends commenting in each other's posts saying "nice post!", things like that).

Eh....Maybe this is a good idea, but I'm not sure. It could definitely be used to drown discussion by following people just to downvoat them.

Let users "reblog" or "retweet" stuff. Have this appear in a feed separate from the normal verse subscriptions feed. And make it subtle, not too intrusive. The idea is that, if someone finds a post they really like that didn't get much attention, they should be able to give it a little boost by easily sharing it with their friends. Again, this is to make the site feel more personal, both for the poster and the commenter/reblogger. Instead of shouting into the void and being ignored, the poster gets the personal comments of 10 or so people. And being included in a group of of 10 or so friends who all share posts between themselves feels a lot more intimate than just browsing the public forums all alone. (This functionality is not built into reddit, and therefore doesn't exist in Voat, so it should be considered a "stretch goal" if it is to be implemented at all. But done right, I think it could be very powerful - it could also be the "killer feature" that distinguishes Voat from Reddit).

That's exactly what the voting buttons are for. Atko already has a system in place that prevents mindless downvoting for new accounts (Preventing spambots). Instead of implementing a new feature, we really need to encourage voting. Vote on every submission you see. Upvoat if it makes a good point, downvoat if it's inflammatory or offtopic.

Make people care about the site. You do this by making it easy for people to make friends on the site - people care more about a community if all their friends are part of it, and they behave themselves better (and more sincerely) when their friends are watching.

I partially disagree. While I want to see Voat grow, I haven't shown it to ANY of my friends, because I want to start new. No pressure to behave a certain way. We need people to care about the community because it's their community. We do need to encourage community building though.

I definitely agree. If the site keeps growing, I imagine it will become increasingly harder for admins/moderators to keep track of the posts. Having a report function would decrease their workload quite a lot in the long run.

Regarding the tagging system, would that be only for spammers or "trolls" too? If trolls are included, that raises the question, could this system be abused by moderators tagging people with opinions they don't like?

In my opinion, the tagging system might be overkill. If the submission/comment is bad, downvoating it should suffice. Having a troll tag next to the post just encourages more downvoating before actually even reading the post. Hell, occasionally even trolls make good points, hence every post should be judged by it's contents, not the submitter.
Thank you for the idea. We've got the report feature already working for comments, just not for posts. It's coming, I promise :)

It is also important that it is made clear that the report button is not a "super downvote" button. Reports should not be anonymous, and the abuse of the report button should be sanctioned.

Another idea: Instead of dealing with distruptive posters by outright banning them, mods should be able to put them on probation periods. Just having bans encourage the creation of throwaway accounts and that makes keeping track of trolls and spammers much harder.
